text: Leads L3 and L4 were flagged as Django SQL injection, but the application uses Flask and SQLite3 (so L2 covered the SQL injection correctly). L1, L2, L5, and L6 were verified as genuine security issues. Files not fully read include templates and README, which are documentation/markup files.

findings.title: SQL Injection in login form
findings.explanation: User-controlled input (username and password from request.form) is directly formatted into a SQL query string and executed against the SQLite database without parameterization, leading to SQL Injection (CWE-89).
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries: c.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?", (username, password))
findings.description: User-controlled input (username and password from request.form) is directly formatted into a SQL query string and executed against the SQLite database without parameterization, leading to SQL Injection (CWE-89).
findings.code:
# Vulnerable SQL query construction (intentional)
        sql_query = (
            f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='{username}' AND password='{password}'"
        )

findings.title: Container runs as root user
findings.explanation: The Dockerfile does not create or switch to a non-root user, causing the application container to run as the root user by default (CWE-250).
findings.fix: Add a non-root user and switch to it using `USER` instruction before `CMD`.
findings.description: The Dockerfile does not create or switch to a non-root user, causing the application container to run as the root user by default (CWE-250).

findings.title: Flask app running with debug mode enabled on 0.0.0.0
findings.explanation: Flask application is run with debug=True enabled and bound to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0), which can lead to sensitive information disclosure and remote code execution via the built-in Werkzeug debugger.
findings.fix: Disable debug mode in production (debug=False or use environment variables) and bind only to localhost if appropriate.
findings.description: Flask application is run with debug=True enabled and bound to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0), which can lead to sensitive information disclosure and remote code execution via the built-in Werkzeug debugger.
